name: piano
_about: A MULTISAMPLED ACOUSTIC PIANO AS A BUILDING BLOCK. The loader and its five laws live in dsp/PianoSamples.h; these are the nine controls a host exposes on top of it. Every one shapes a RECORDING rather than modelling a string, which is the honest description and the reason they are [EAR] - a sampled piano cannot re-strike a string, so each control is the audible consequence of its name applied to the sample. For the modelled alternative see dspblocks/include/dsp/PianoString.h, which is a different instrument.
_ids: LOCAL names. A host maps them to its own frozen ids in one adapter, as Solera does in Source/Steinway.h.

params.name: Model
params._meaning: WHICH RECORDING SET. One folder each, and the list is what can actually be had: the University of Iowa's Steinway (public domain) and two FreePats sets (CC0). A Bosendorfer and a Yamaha C7 were researched and are NOT obtainable under a free licence, so they are not offered - a window naming an instrument the machine does not have is a lie the player cannot see through.
params.provenance: [REF] the three sets' own pages, named in each folder's README

params._meaning: STRETCH TUNING, and the only one of the nine that belongs in the PITCH sum rather than after it. A real piano is tuned wide - the top sharp, the bottom flat, nothing in the middle - because the strings are stiff and their partials are not exact multiples. At 0 the keyboard is equal-tempered, which is what a sampler normally gives and is not what a piano sounds like.
params.provenance: [EAR] the amount; the shape is the Railsback curve's

params._meaning: How long a held note rings, as a scale on the recording's own decay.
The damper, and it only touches a note the key has LET GO of - that is what a damper is. A held note is unchanged, which is why a gate that holds the note measures this as dead.
A hard hammer is bright and a soft one is not. A one-pole on the sample, open at 1.
Where the hammer strikes decides which partial is missing: a string struck at 1/n has no nth harmonic. That is a comb, and a comb is what this is.
params.provenance: [EAR] the depth; the missing-partial law is the string's own

params._meaning: The body the strings are mounted on, which rings with everything played. Three low resonances.
A piano note is two or three strings very slightly apart, and that beat is most of why a piano sounds alive rather than like one string. A second read of the same sample, detuned a few cents.
A release that falls fast and then slowly, which is what a real damper does: it grabs, then the remaining energy leaks away. Acts only after the key is released, with `damping`.
params.provenance: [EAR], and the name is the Alesis Andromeda A6's for the same shape

samples._about: What the host puts in a folder. One folder per model.
samples.naming: Piano.<dyn>.<note>.<ext>, dyn one of pp/mf/ff, note spelled with flats (Bb4), ext flac preferred and wav read as a fallback.
samples.keys: 21 to 108, A0 to C8. A key with no recording is transposed from the nearest that has one; it is never borrowed from another dynamic unless that dynamic is entirely empty.
samples.layers: Three is the design. A set with one or two leaves the others empty and the loader serves them from the nearest populated side, preferring the softer.
